title: Disability Across Cultures: A Human-Centered Audit of Ableism in Western and Indic LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting Western and Indic large language models (LLMs) to rate the toxicity and ableism of a curated dataset of social media comments on a 0-10 scale and explain their reasoning, then comparing these outputs to ground-truth ratings and qualitative explanations from People with Disabilities (PwD) in the US and India.

Comparing harm assessments between Western and Indic LLMs, testing model sensitivity using demographic prompting (e.g., adding context like 'in India'), and contrasting model interpretations against the localized, cross-cultural lived experiences and norms of US and Indian PwD.

Translating the ableist speech dataset into Hindi and comparing how models rate toxicity and ableism across English, Hindi Casual, and Hindi Formal registers to evaluate consistency in harm detection across languages and formality levels.
